title: Clear out stale documentation; README for a prospective club
description: Most of docs/ is planning history or the author's runbooks, and several files are wrong (Docker Compose v1 commands, S3 backup claims, LevelDB-era steps, Go-first getting started, stale test counts). Move history to docs/archive/ with a one-line index, delete what is simply wrong and superseded, and rewrite README.md for a prospective club: what it is, who it is for (BHPLTA clubs), what you get including club championships, a screenshot or two from demo data, and 'Install' pointing at the new guide. Update CONTRIBUTING.md's club adaptation section, CLAUDE.md, docs/README.md and the sprints index. Remove the duplicate import scripts in scripts/ that the app now replaces.

recommended_model.name: Sonnet 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Editorial clean-up with a clear target state.

acceptance_criteria: docs/ top level contains only current, accurate documents; history is under docs/archive/
README.md opens with what a club gets and how to install, in under two screens
No tracked document contradicts shipped behaviour on install, database, backups or sign-in
CLAUDE.md reflects embedded assets, SQLite-only, the CLI subcommands, roles and the test suites as they are
scripts/ contains only scripts that are still used, each with a header comment
Root-level PROFILE_IMPLEMENTATION.md and COURTHIVE_SETUP.md are archived or removed
testing_requirements: Link check across all Markdown files

context.user_story: As someone deciding whether to adopt this, I want the front page to tell me what it is and how to start.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
